knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 2.1.3
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly describes probability and quantile evaluation for a named univariate distribution?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Univariate probability and quantile work uses the one-dimensional CDF or survival function. Recognition alone is not evaluation, and joint machinery is not the primary move for a single named univariate family.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Use CDF/survival for probabilities; invert CDF for quantiles on a named univariate family.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating family recognition as finished evaluation, or pulling joint steps into a univariate task.

choices.label: For a placed univariate family, evaluate a probability such as P(X > x) from the CDF or survival function, and evaluate a quantile by inverting the CDF to solve F(x) = p for x.
Naming the distribution family (for example Exponential) completes probability and quantile evaluation; no calculation is required once the family is recognised.
A quantile is always the sample mean of the distribution; probabilities are read directly from a joint table of (X, Y).
Probability evaluation for univariate X requires first obtaining marginals by summing out Y from a joint distribution.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 2.1.3
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Claim sizes are Exponential with mean θ = 1000. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Compute P(X > 2000) and the 90th percentile; refuse recognition-as-evaluation.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Survival gives e^{-2000/1000}. Quantile inversion gives 1000 ln(10). Halving by mean ratio, scaling the mean by 0.9, or stopping at recognition are all wrong.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Heuristic mean ratios, linear scaling of the mean for quantiles, or recognition without calculation.

choices.label: P(X > 2000) = e^{-2} ≈ 0.135. The 90th percentile solves 1 − e^{-x/1000} = 0.9, giving x = 1000 ln(10) ≈ 2302.6. Naming Exponential does not replace these calculations.
P(X > 2000) = 0.5 because the threshold 2000 is twice the mean 1000, so the tail probability is one half.
The 90th percentile is 900 because 0.9 × 1000 = 900 for any Exponential with mean θ.
Once the model is Exponential(θ = 1000), probability and quantile questions are answered by naming the family; numeric evaluation is optional decoration.
